Transportation
Rental Car · LAX
With six travelers plus luggage, a 7-passenger minivan or full-size SUV is the right call — picked up at LAX on June 26 at 1:00 PM, returned July 1 at 1:15 PM. Sized for the whole group and the bags, easy in and out for the seniors and the kids.

Minivan / Full-Size SUV

Agent Notes: Late June is summer peak at LAX, and minivans/7-pax SUVs are the highest-demand class in summer — book 3–4 weeks out to lock the lowest rate. Typical vehicles in this class: Chrysler Pacifica, Toyota Sienna, Honda Odyssey on the minivan side, or Chevy Tahoe, Ford Expedition, Toyota Highlander on the SUV side. Alamo, Hertz, and National have the strongest LAX availability for this class. All LAX rental companies operate from the off-terminal CONRAC — free shuttle, about 10 minutes from any terminal. Taxes, airport fees, and the California CFC add roughly $70–$100 on top of the base rate for a 5-day rental — always compare the final total, not the daily headline rate. For the group: minivan has lower step-in (better for the seniors), more interior room, and easier sliding doors in parking lots; SUV sits higher (better visibility), handles luggage on the roof rack, and feels more substantial on the freeway. Either works — minivan is generally cheaper.

✨ The Two Choices in Plain Numbers
Express costs $960 MORE than BOGO — and gives you HALF the park days. That premium buys time inside the park, not more time at the park.
BOGO Fine Print: Both visits must be completed on or before December 16, 2026. The 2nd visit cannot fall on certain blockout dates (July 3, 4, 25; Sept 5, 6, 12, 19, 26; Oct 3, 10, 17, 24; Nov 27, 28) — none of these affect Barbara's trip window, so back-to-back days on June 29 & 30 work perfectly. Each person in the group needs their own BOGO ticket (not transferable). The 2nd visit doesn't have to be consecutive — if they only have energy for one day in LA, they can technically save the 2nd visit for a return trip, but most authorized vendor terms require the 2nd visit within 7 days of the first, so plan to use both during this trip.

Universal Express Pass · How It Works

Worth understanding before you decide. It's a real upgrade for some groups, overkill for others.

✓ What's Included
• Park admission (separate ticket NOT required)
• One-time Express lane access at every ride, attraction, and seated show
• Reservation-free entry to Super Nintendo World (no virtual line needed)
• Priority seating at WaterWorld & other shows
⚠ The Catch
• Express access is one use per ride — re-ride your favorite using standby
• Same price for adults & kids ages 3+ (no child discount)
• Express can sell out on peak days — sometimes before the gate opens
• Doesn't include parking or food
📊 The Time Math
On peak days, standby lines for the headliners (Mario Kart, Forbidden Journey, Studio Tour, Fast & Furious) routinely hit 60–90 minutes each. Express drops those waits to under 10 minutes. Across a full park day, that's 3–5 hours saved — enough to fit everything into one day instead of stretching across two.
Express Pass: When the $960 Premium Earns Its Keep

It's a good fit if: The seniors don't want to stand in long lines, the kids have limited line patience, the group would rather have one well-done day at Universal so they can use Tuesday for something else (a beach day, Santa Monica, etc.), OR they want to ride absolutely everything without rushing.

It's probably not worth it if: The group is OK with standing in lines, they want a relaxed pace, OR they'd rather spend two leisurely days in the park enjoying the atmosphere (especially Wizarding World and Super Nintendo World, which are more fun when you're not rushing through them).

The dollar math vs BOGO: Express is $1,854 for the group; BOGO is $894. That's a $960 premium for ONE park day instead of TWO. The premium buys time inside the park (skipping 60–90 min lines) — it doesn't buy more days at the park.

One more angle: Express also gives back a full day of the trip. Without it, Universal eats both Monday and Tuesday. With it, Universal is one day (Monday) and Tuesday becomes a flex day for the beach, Hollywood, or just rest before flying out Wednesday. For some families, that day of breathing room is worth more than the $960.

Booking note: Buy online in advance — gate-day prices run $10–$20/person higher, and Express does sell out on peak summer days. Monday/Tuesday are lower-risk than a weekend, but still book ahead.

Best Days & Times to Go

When you go matters as much as how you tour.

📅 Recommended Days
Mon June 29 & Tues June 30
Universal weekends in summer are chaos. Weekdays in summer are still busy but noticeably calmer. Tuesday tends to be the lightest day of the week.
⏰ Recommended Arrival
8:30 AM (30 min before gate)
Late June park hours: 9 AM – 9 or 10 PM. The first 2 hours are the magic window — half the wait times of mid-afternoon. Don't sleep in.

Don't-Miss Attractions

★ = absolute must-do. The park is split between Upper Lot (entrance level) and Lower Lot (down a long escalator).

Upper Lot

Park entrance level
  • World-Famous Studio Tour THE signature attraction. 45–60 min tram through working backlots, Jaws, Earthquake, more.
  • Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey Inside Hogwarts Castle. The Wizarding World's headliner.
  • Flight of the Hippogriff Family-friendly Wizarding World coaster.
  • Ollivanders Wand Experience ~5–10 min interactive wand-choosing ceremony. Lines build fast.
  • Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift NEW summer 2026 — first outdoor coaster at the park, 72 mph. Expect peak crowds.
  • Secret Life of Pets: Off the Leash Excellent newer dark ride — great for the 8-year-old.
  • WaterWorld Stunt Show 20-min live show, multiple times daily.
  • DreamWorks Theatre: Kung Fu Panda Indoor 4D theater experience.
  • Despicable Me Minion Mayhem Family-friendly motion simulator.

Lower Lot

Down four long escalators
  • Super Nintendo World An entire land. Includes Mario Kart: Bowser's Challenge (the headliner), Yoshi's Adventure, mini-games throughout, Toadstool Cafe, 1-UP Factory shop.
  • Mario Kart: Bowser's Challenge AR-meets-physical-track ride. Massive crowd draw — get there early or use Virtual Line.
  • Yoshi's Adventure Slow family ride inside Super Nintendo World.
  • Jurassic World: The Ride Featuring the new Indominus Rex. You will get wet — bring a poncho or sit center.
  • Transformers: The Ride 3D Intense motion-simulator dark ride.
  • Revenge of the Mummy Indoor coaster — short but punchy.

The 2-Day Split Plan (Recommended)

If you take the BOGO deal — and you should — here's how to split the park between two days. Anchor each day to one lot, and do not bounce back and forth between Upper and Lower or you'll waste an hour on those escalators.

💡 Practical Tips That Save Real Time:

1. Download the Universal Studios Hollywood app before you go. Wait times in real time, virtual line for Super Nintendo World when it's active, mobile food ordering.
2. The escalators between Upper & Lower Lot are a 5–7 minute commute each way. That's the #1 reason rookie visitors run out of day — plan each lot as a dedicated block.
3. Single Rider lines are available at Mario Kart, Transformers, Jurassic World, Mummy, and Forbidden Journey. If the group doesn't mind splitting up, single riders cut waits 30–60%.
4. Express Pass is the alternative path — covered in full above. Two doors: BOGO buys you time, Express buys you comfort. Either works; group decides.
5. Park is cashless. Tap/swipe only.
6. Parking is ~$35/day general, ~$45 prime — pay each visit. Free CityWalk parking after 6 PM for evening visits only.
